## Summary

Add `--quantization mxfp_w4a8` support for Ascend MoE experts and completion-tracked loading for online W4A8 Linear/MoE weights. FP16/BF16 weights are converted to packed MXFP4 as each logical weight finishes loading, then run with MXFP8 activations. Pre-quantized ModelSlim checkpoints keep their existing path.

## Scope

This PR is limited to online W4A8 functionality, loading lifecycle, and explicit FP4 weight policy. The later TP routing-fusion/threshold and GDN input-reuse experiments have been archived and removed from this PR. Performance optimization will be handled separately; no serving speedup is claimed here.

The feature branch was restored to `3cdd0182b9dbb18c336594564fb7b98a2d97f87a` and merged with upstream main `9e9296fdf352d767e66d49367b8763fd788184b6`. The current head is `c0e0fab8e6a039793782c6be92a7f0b245d32212`. The general local-K/per-matmul fixes identified during #32602 review now live in this prerequisite PR. Its separate #36426 validation branch was updated in the same round; #32602 inherits these fixes via an ordinary merge. No W4A4 feature or #36426 patch was brought into this PR.

## Changes

- Allocate floating-point source weights lazily, preserve native TP/EP shard loading, and quantize Linear weights and MoE W13/W2 independently when their local shards are complete. Release source backing storage even when a caller retains an old Parameter handle.
- Validate completion during post-load processing, reject duplicate/incomplete loads, and support reloads through registered weight loaders. Reuse `CopyNumelCounter`.
- Explicitly use `round_mode="rint", scale_alg=2, dst_type_max=7.25` for online Linear/MoE FP4 weights. Do not copy those settings into MXFP8 activation quantization or requantize offline packed weights; W4A4 is unchanged.
- Reuse upstream W4A8 grouped matmuls, prepared weight/scale layouts and dispatcher contracts. Support the `auto` and `ascend` MoE runners.
- Handle Dense A8W4 bias and retain floating-point fallback for non-aligned Linear layers. Check local K using the bound TP group for RowParallelLinear before `input_size_per_partition` exists; Column/replicated layers do not divide K by TP.
- Make runner construction and execution both consult W13 for gmm1 fusion. Add keyword-only `weight_prefix` to the W4A8 kernel while preserving its existing positional quant-policy argument. Online, ModelSlim, compressed-tensors, DeepSeek FP4 and FP8-config FP4-expert entrypoints bind W13/W2 explicitly; W2 no longer creates a fused component. Weight/activation policies and layouts are unchanged.
- Resolve concrete post-load device aliases before residency checks, avoiding unsupported restore copies of already-resident NZ views while retaining real cross-device staging.
- Preserve upstream EPLB all-local-replica/shared-slot filtering. Adapt its stand-in test fixture to the extracted `_weight_loader_expert_ids` helper.

## Usage and references

Use an unquantized FP16/BF16 checkpoint with `--quantization mxfp_w4a8`. No separate `--online-quantization` flag is added.

Replaces #32601 and uses the merged #32745 fixes. Ascend 950 Qwen3.5 requires a compatible Gemma kernel wheel/API containing [sgl-kernel-npu#638](https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-kernel-npu/pull/638).

The loading lifecycle is adapted from #29048; it is a reference, not a merge dependency. The FP4 weight policy follows #43367. #44738 covers a separate diffusion W8A8 path.

## Validation

At the refreshed head:

- **48 import-isolated CPU checks passed; 7 CUDA-dependent checks skipped**, on both the feature and combination branches. This includes native shard-loader/Parameter contracts, source release and reloads, weight-policy/layout checks, post-load staging, and 8 upstream EPLB weight-loading tests.
- NPU operations were mocked and unrelated serving imports isolated. The standard test entrypoint remains blocked locally by missing `orjson`; these checks are not full-package or NPU end-to-end validation.
- Applicable Ruff checks, formatting, isort, codespell, Python syntax, test registration and PR-diff checks passed. Six earlier injected contract regressions were detected by the isolated checks. Four additional injections covering local K, the runner fusion decision, W2 allocation and online prefix wiring were also detected.
- Consolidated four new test files into two: shared W4A8 Linear/MoE contracts and loading lifecycle tests. Existing post-load and EPLB coverage stays in its original files. Unrelated ModelSlim name-resolution/allocation tests were removed; online/offline preparation is still checked through the real entrypoint.

### Loading-stage peak memory (user-reported, October 30)

The deployment user supplied paired results from the standalone online W4A8 loading-memory collector (`mxfp_w4a8`). Both reported records are TP rank 0 / logical device 0 / target and have status **ok**, indicating complete measured `ModelRunner.load_model` windows.

- Before: `493372ce8fee`, the direct parent of loading-lifecycle change `ab8f7cd9ce`; online W4A8 is already supported, with quantization deferred until post-load.
- After: `c0e0fab8e6a0`, the current formal PR head, without the separate #36426 combination patch.

| NPU allocator metric | Before (GiB) | After (GiB) | Reduction |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Peak allocated | 65.964 | 20.603 | **45.361 GiB / 68.77%** |
| Peak reserved | 66.129 | 20.869 | **45.260 GiB / 68.44%** |
| Allocated at load end | 19.495 | 19.494 | 0.001 GiB |
| Reserved at load end | 20.156 | 19.869 | 0.287 GiB |

Percentages use the rounded summary values. The loading peak decreased substantially while end-of-load allocation stayed approximately constant, consistent with reducing transient loading residency rather than substantially changing the final resident footprint.

**Measurement scope:** the same collector synchronizes and resets NPU allocator peaks at each worker's `ModelRunner.load_model` entry, then synchronizes and reads the counters when the method returns. The window includes construction, weight loading and post-load preparation, but excludes subsequent KV-pool allocation, graph capture and serving warmup. These are **loading-stage allocator peaks, not total-device HBM or whole-startup peaks**.

This is user-reported deployment evidence, not a locally executed NPU test. The version pair also includes upstream synchronization, weight-policy changes and later fixes, so it is not a loader-only ablation or a per-source-buffer lifetime trace. Full configuration, software and physical-device mapping remain in the original JSON reports/server logs and were not included in the pasted summary. No inference-memory, warmup/request, accuracy or throughput result is implied by these measurements.

User-reported hardware evaluation, received before this refresh:

| Evaluation | BF16 | Online W4A8 |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| GSM8K | 96.13 | 96.13 |

The scores match at the reported precision. Per-run SHAs and raw evaluation configuration/logs were not attached, so this is recorded as deployment-user feedback, not a fresh evaluation of the post-merge head or proof of model-wide numerical equivalence. The earlier Ascend 950 weight-policy probe reported improved reconstruction error on 40/40 sampled weights; that sample-level result is separate from GSM8K.

This avoids retaining the full floating-point model, but still stages complete logical W13/W2 tensors. Please verify source release and startup peak memory on NPU.

Thanks for the detailed guidance. The loading-lifecycle changes are implemented and retained in the refreshed head `d48ccd511607ee608e2c3b294dacc8756b330208`:

- Linear and MoE source weights start as meta placeholders and materialize lazily; the native TP/EP shard loaders still perform slicing and expert placement.
- Linear weights and MoE W13/W2 convert independently when each logical local tensor is complete. Nonlocal experts do not materialize a source or initiate a reload.
- Conversion releases the floating-point backing storage even when the caller retains an old Parameter handle. Post-load processing validates completion, rejects duplicate/incomplete/bypassed loads, and permits reloads through the registered loaders.
- Selection uses `mxfp_w4a8`; FP4 packing, UE8M0 scales and the existing W4A8 kernels are retained, without adopting the integer-mode flag or INT4 scale encoding from #29048.

The latest main has also been merged. Its all-local-replica EPLB fix is retained, including filtering routed slots before mapping shared slots; the corresponding upstream test fixture now binds `_weight_loader_expert_ids`.

detail.body:
## Summary

Add `--quantization mxfp_w4a8` support for Ascend MoE experts and completion-tracked loading for online W4A8 Linear/MoE weights. FP16/BF16 weights are converted to packed MXFP4 as each logical weight finishes loading, then run with MXFP8 activations. Pre-quantized ModelSlim checkpoints keep their existing path.

## Scope

This PR is limited to online W4A8 functionality, loading lifecycle, and explicit FP4 weight policy. The later TP routing-fusion/threshold and GDN input-reuse experiments have been archived and removed from this PR. Performance optimization will be handled separately; no serving speedup is claimed here.

The feature branch was restored to `3cdd0182b9dbb18c336594564fb7b98a2d97f87a` and merged with upstream main `9e9296fdf352d767e66d49367b8763fd788184b6`. The current head is `c0e0fab8e6a039793782c6be92a7f0b245d32212`. The general local-K/per-matmul fixes identified during #32602 review now live in this prerequisite PR. Its separate #36426 validation branch was updated in the same round; #32602 inherits these fixes via an ordinary merge. No W4A4 feature or #36426 patch was brought into this PR.

## Changes

- Allocate floating-point source weights lazily, preserve native TP/EP shard loading, and quantize Linear weights and MoE W13/W2 independently when their local shards are complete. Release source backing storage even when a caller retains an old Parameter handle.
- Validate completion during post-load processing, reject duplicate/incomplete loads, and support reloads through registered weight loaders. Reuse `CopyNumelCounter`.
- Explicitly use `round_mode="rint", scale_alg=2, dst_type_max=7.25` for online Linear/MoE FP4 weights. Do not copy those settings into MXFP8 activation quantization or requantize offline packed weights; W4A4 is unchanged.
- Reuse upstream W4A8 grouped matmuls, prepared weight/scale layouts and dispatcher contracts. Support the `auto` and `ascend` MoE runners.
- Handle Dense A8W4 bias and retain floating-point fallback for non-aligned Linear layers. Check local K using the bound TP group for RowParallelLinear before `input_size_per_partition` exists; Column/replicated layers do not divide K by TP.
- Make runner construction and execution both consult W13 for gmm1 fusion. Add keyword-only `weight_prefix` to the W4A8 kernel while preserving its existing positional quant-policy argument. Online, ModelSlim, compressed-tensors, DeepSeek FP4 and FP8-config FP4-expert entrypoints bind W13/W2 explicitly; W2 no longer creates a fused component. Weight/activation policies and layouts are unchanged.
- Resolve concrete post-load device aliases before residency checks, avoiding unsupported restore copies of already-resident NZ views while retaining real cross-device staging.
- Preserve upstream EPLB all-local-replica/shared-slot filtering. Adapt its stand-in test fixture to the extracted `_weight_loader_expert_ids` helper.

## Usage and references

Use an unquantized FP16/BF16 checkpoint with `--quantization mxfp_w4a8`. No separate `--online-quantization` flag is added.

Replaces #32601 and uses the merged #32745 fixes. Ascend 950 Qwen3.5 requires a compatible Gemma kernel wheel/API containing [sgl-kernel-npu#638](https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-kernel-npu/pull/638).

The loading lifecycle is adapted from #29048; it is a reference, not a merge dependency. The FP4 weight policy follows #43367. #44738 covers a separate diffusion W8A8 path.

## Validation

At the refreshed head:

- **48 import-isolated CPU checks passed; 7 CUDA-dependent checks skipped**, on both the feature and combination branches. This includes native shard-loader/Parameter contracts, source release and reloads, weight-policy/layout checks, post-load staging, and 8 upstream EPLB weight-loading tests.
- NPU operations were mocked and unrelated serving imports isolated. The standard test entrypoint remains blocked locally by missing `orjson`; these checks are not full-package or NPU end-to-end validation.
- Applicable Ruff checks, formatting, isort, codespell, Python syntax, test registration and PR-diff checks passed. Six earlier injected contract regressions were detected by the isolated checks. Four additional injections covering local K, the runner fusion decision, W2 allocation and online prefix wiring were also detected.
- Consolidated four new test files into two: shared W4A8 Linear/MoE contracts and loading lifecycle tests. Existing post-load and EPLB coverage stays in its original files. Unrelated ModelSlim name-resolution/allocation tests were removed; online/offline preparation is still checked through the real entrypoint.

### Loading-stage peak memory (user-reported, October 30)

The deployment user supplied paired results from the standalone online W4A8 loading-memory collector (`mxfp_w4a8`). Both reported records are TP rank 0 / logical device 0 / target and have status **ok**, indicating complete measured `ModelRunner.load_model` windows.

- Before: `493372ce8fee`, the direct parent of loading-lifecycle change `ab8f7cd9ce`; online W4A8 is already supported, with quantization deferred until post-load.
- After: `c0e0fab8e6a0`, the current formal PR head, without the separate #36426 combination patch.

| NPU allocator metric | Before (GiB) | After (GiB) | Reduction |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Peak allocated | 65.964 | 20.603 | **45.361 GiB / 68.77%** |
| Peak reserved | 66.129 | 20.869 | **45.260 GiB / 68.44%** |
| Allocated at load end | 19.495 | 19.494 | 0.001 GiB |
| Reserved at load end | 20.156 | 19.869 | 0.287 GiB |

Percentages use the rounded summary values. The loading peak decreased substantially while end-of-load allocation stayed approximately constant, consistent with reducing transient loading residency rather than substantially changing the final resident footprint.

**Measurement scope:** the same collector synchronizes and resets NPU allocator peaks at each worker's `ModelRunner.load_model` entry, then synchronizes and reads the counters when the method returns. The window includes construction, weight loading and post-load preparation, but excludes subsequent KV-pool allocation, graph capture and serving warmup. These are **loading-stage allocator peaks, not total-device HBM or whole-startup peaks**.

This is user-reported deployment evidence, not a locally executed NPU test. The version pair also includes upstream synchronization, weight-policy changes and later fixes, so it is not a loader-only ablation or a per-source-buffer lifetime trace. Full configuration, software and physical-device mapping remain in the original JSON reports/server logs and were not included in the pasted summary. No inference-memory, warmup/request, accuracy or throughput result is implied by these measurements.

User-reported hardware evaluation, received before this refresh:

| Evaluation | BF16 | Online W4A8 |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| GSM8K | 96.13 | 96.13 |

The scores match at the reported precision. Per-run SHAs and raw evaluation configuration/logs were not attached, so this is recorded as deployment-user feedback, not a fresh evaluation of the post-merge head or proof of model-wide numerical equivalence. The earlier Ascend 950 weight-policy probe reported improved reconstruction error on 40/40 sampled weights; that sample-level result is separate from GSM8K.

Hi! Thank you for your PR! I have some suggestions to improve it:

1. The default loader still creates the full local FP16/BF16 model before quantization, so a model whose MXFP4 weights fit can still run out of memory during loading.

Could we adapt the completion-tracked loading from #29048 (i already implement it and test on w8a8_int/w4a4_int)? The relevant parts at `656693189c6d` are:

- [`NPUOnlineDenseWeightLoader`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/656693189c6d19c853024f3e045c3c563c50b782/python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/npu/quantization/online_quantization.py#L163): lazy allocation and conversion once the logical dense weight is complete.
- [`NPUOnlineMoEWeightLoader`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/656693189c6d19c853024f3e045c3c563c50b782/python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/npu/quantization/online_quantization.py#L271): independent W13/W2 completion tracking, nonlocal-expert filtering, and conversion during loading.
- [Meta-backed MoE allocation and loader registration](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/656693189c6d19c853024f3e045c3c563c50b782/python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/unquant.py#L699), plus the [expert-routing helper](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/656693189c6d19c853024f3e045c3c563c50b782/python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/fused_moe_triton/layer.py#L1040).
- [Post-load completion/reload checks](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/656693189c6d19c853024f3e045c3c563c50b782/python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/npu/quantization/moe_methods.py#L1069), so the final pass validates prepared weights instead of preparing them again.

Only the loading lifecycle should be adapted. Keep this PR's FP4 packing, UE8M0 scales, and W4A8 kernels; #29048's integer quantization and INT4 scale encoding do not apply. The loader also needs to select this PR's `mxfp_w4a8` config rather than #29048's integer-mode flag.

This avoids retaining the full floating-point model, but still stages complete logical W13/W2 tensors. Please verify source release and startup peak memory on NPU.

### Accuracy failure

`TestDSV41FlashTrtllmBoundedBCG.test_mmmu_pro` runs CUDA/TRTLLM with FlashInfer MXFP4, not the NPU W4A8 computation added here. The shared changes reorganize expert-ID loading and normalize post-load device staging; they do not change this path's inference arithmetic.

The evaluation explicitly uses **`temperature=1.0`, `seed=None`, and 200 examples**. The same test scored [0.760 on main](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/40970965852/job/123787535076), [0.770 in another main run](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41045755944/job/124029582438), and [0.795 on PR #44442](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41000090922/job/124001628973). Here, 0.740 is only two correct answers below the threshold. **Sampling variance is the more likely explanation than a regression from these changes**; this is an attribution based on the evaluation settings and code paths, not a claim of a fixed-seed numerical comparison.
